artifacts.summary: Corrects and grounds the task's WORK-item scope against a live check-extension-docs.sh run: true description count is 147 (not 166), tags rename applies to only 6 of the 10 named extensions, WORK item 5's blanket 'safe to delete' premise has an exception (memory-troubleshooting.md), core (9 entries, 1 needing a replacement agents hook) and email (1 entry) are also in scope for load_when.skills deletion beyond what WORK item 5 names, formal has 40 load_when.topics violations not named in any WORK item, and founder's 11 entries need an array-union merge rather than an overwrite for WORK item 3.

memory_candidates.content: When a task description gives concrete WORK-item counts/scope for a mechanical migration (e.g. '166 entries', 'same 10 extensions'), re-derive those counts live against the actual gate/validator (e.g. check-extension-docs.sh's own advisory-line counts) rather than trusting the task description's summary numbers -- this task's description undercounted (166 vs actual 147) and overscoped (claimed tags exists in 10 extensions when it's really 6), and separately omitted 3 real violation sources (core's load_when.skills, email's 1 load_when.skills entry, formal's load_when.topics nesting) that are required by the verification bar but not named in any WORK item.

Before a blind field-deletion migration (e.g. deleting load_when.skills across many entries), check each entry's OTHER load_when keys individually -- a blanket per-extension justification ('these entries already carry non-empty commands') can still have per-entry exceptions. In this codebase, project/memory/memory-troubleshooting.md and core/patterns/lit-stage4a-flow.md each had skills as their ONLY reachability hook, so deleting skills without adding a replacement (commands or agents respectively) would have orphaned them from context-discovery.md's adaptive jq query.
